source: sa_matsyapurANa1-176.txt; GRETIL (gretil.sub.uni-goettingen.de), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (data entry: Oliver Hellwig)
reply:
Only a few verses state kinship or succession directly.

- [47.244] says Rāma was born as Daśaratha's son (daśarathātmajaḥ).
- [47.245] says Vedavyāsa was born from Parāśara (parāśarāt). I did not mark this as begotten_by, since the text does not count him as another man's child.
- [47.247] gives Kalkī as "viṣṇuyaśasaḥ", which names Viṣṇuyaśas but only in a loose way, and I left it out as too ambiguous.
- [47.263] introduces the lines of Turvasu, Pūru, Druhyu and Anu, but it only announces what will be told and states no relation, so I left it out.

Rāma in 47.244 is named alone as "rāmo", and the verse also calls him the seventh incarnation. That is clear enough to give as son_of Daśaratha.
